Mark the randomisation/allocation point in a criteria pipeline

Source: R/criteria.R
randomise.Rd

randomise() records where allocation happens in the pipeline without excluding any rows (n_fail is always 0). as_consort_diagram() and as_attrition_tibble() use its by/arms to default branch_by when not explicitly supplied, and steps at or after it are flagged post_randomisation in as_attrition_tibble()'s output.

Usage

randomise(criteria, by, arms, label = "Randomised", category = NULL)

Arguments

criteria

A cf_criteria object (or NULL to start a new one).

by

One or more column names (character vector) naming the randomisation unit (e.g. "cluster_id" for cluster randomisation, or the participant id for individual randomisation).

arms

A single column name (string) holding each unit's allocated arm (e.g. "arm").

label

A short human-readable description of this step. Default "Randomised" (unlike other builders, a label is not required).

category

An optional string grouping this step with others for display. NULL leaves it uncategorised.

Value

The updated cf_criteria object.

See also

Other criteria builders: cf_criteria(), cf_criterion(), check_criteria(), exclude(), group_exclude(), group_include(), include(), select_within()

Examples

cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ eligible, label = "Eligible clusters") |>
  randomise(by = "cluster_id", arms = "arm") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew after allocation")
#> Cohort criteria pipeline  (3 steps)
#>    1. [+][~] (include) Eligible clusters
#>           eligible
#>    2. [R][-] (randomise) [by: cluster_id] [arms: arm] Randomised
#>           <none>
#>    3. [-][~] (exclude) Withdrew after allocation
#>           withdrew
